title: Google adopted the system. It didn't invent it.
description:
Google adopted the system. It didn't invent it. By the time OKRs reached Google, the method had already been running inside another company for decades.

Built the system inside Intel and called it 'iMBOs', Intel Management by Objectives, drawing on Peter Drucker's older idea of managing by objectives from the 1950s.

John Doerr joined Intel in 1974 as a salesman and sat in Grove's internal course in 1975, where he first learned the iMBOs method. He later wrote the book that gave it its modern name: 'Measure What Matters.'

How long the method had already been running at Intel before Doerr, by then a venture capitalist, introduced it to Google's founders in 1999.

When Doerr left Intel for the venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins in 1980, Grove told him venture capital 'is not a real job. It's like being a real estate agent.' Grove wrote the method down just once, in his 1983 book 'High Output Management.'
